title: How to Buy & Redeem Etihad Guest Miles
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Buy Etihad Guest miles to redeem for cheap flights with Etihad and its partner airlines. Photo: Etihad.
Etihad Guest miles are a unique currency because they can be redeemed for flights on around 30 different airlines.
Etihad has partner airlines spanning all three global airline alliances – plus many others that aren’t in any alliance, and therefore aren’t otherwise accessible through Australian frequent flyer or loyalty programs. These include Air Serbia, Maldivian, Hainan Airlines and Starlux.
Buying Etihad Guest miles could be lucrative if you plan to redeem them for flights that are worth more than the cost of the miles (e.g. in Business Class). Etihad Guest is also one of the only programs you can use to book Etihad Airways Business or First Class reward flights more than 30 days before departure .
This guide explains how to buy and redeem Etihad Guest miles – and where you’ll find the best value.
How to buy Etihad Guest miles
You can buy Etihad Guest miles on the Etihad Guest website . You’ll be prompted to log into your account, then taken to the Points.com Storefront page where you can select the number of miles you wish to buy and enter your credit card payment details.
You can buy Etihad Guest miles on Etihad’s website.
If you’re not already a member, you can join Etihad Guest online for free.
The normal price for Etihad Guest miles is USD20 (~AU$29) per thousand, although you can sometimes get miles at a discount ( see below ).
There is an annual purchase limit for most Etihad Guest members of 200,000 miles, or 300,000 miles for Etihad Guest Platinum members. These limits exclude any bonus miles.
Etihad’s website states that miles will normally credit to your account within 24 hours of purchasing them. In our experience, it can take 24-48 hours.
As your transaction will be completed in US Dollars and processed in the United States, you may prefer to pay using a credit card with no international transaction fees to avoid paying a foreign currency surcharge to your bank. You may also like to contact your bank before completing the payment so that your bank doesn’t block your account if they think it’s a suspicious transaction. (It’s not a suspicious transaction, but in the past we have heard of some banks making this assumption and therefore blocking transactions.)
In addition to buying miles outright, you can pay to “boost” the number of miles earned from Etihad Airways flights, Etihad Guest payment cards, hotels, car rentals or with other program partners using the MilesBooster feature .
Special deals on buying Etihad Guest miles
Etihad Guest offers bonus miles or discounts on purchases of Etihad Guest miles during limited-time promotions. These usually take place a few times per year.
Etihad Guest offers aren’t generally quite as generous as those of frequent flyer programs like Avianca LifeMiles , which regularly gives around 145% bonus miles! In the past Etihad’s loyalty program has been known to offer up to 70% bonus miles on purchases, but more recent offers have been closer to a 30% bonus.
You can discuss Etihad “buy miles” promotions on the Australian Frequent Flyer forum:
Join the discussion about Etihad Guest promotions on the AFF forum
Other ways to earn Etihad Guest miles
Of course, buying Etihad Guest miles is not the only way to increase your balance. You can earn miles in many other ways including flying with Etihad and its partner airlines, or by transferring points from a hotel loyalty program.
Redeeming Etihad Guest miles
Etihad has a common award chart for flights on partner airlines, and “from” pricing for Etihad’s own flights. Prices are on a per-sector basis, meaning connecting itineraries are charged as the sum of each individual flight.
Redemptions on Etihad Airways
Etihad no longer publishes an award chart for travel on its own aircraft. However, the below table shows the lowest mileage cost you could expect to pay for a one-way “Value” award, based on the miles flown:
According to Etihad, a “premium redemption fare will be applied based on demand and availability”. In other words, the Etihad website sometimes shows higher redemption prices than what’s listed in its award chart. So, these seem to just be “starting” prices.
Full dynamic pricing applies to OpenSeat awards, which aren’t subject to the same availability restrictions as GuestSeat awards.
So, you should check availability and pricing for your specific redemption before committing to buying miles.
You can also check the minimum miles needed for an award ticket (or upgrade) any specific Etihad Airways route using the Miles Calculator on Etihad’s website .
Note that taxes and fuel surcharges are also payable, in addition to the miles. Etihad imposes relatively high fuel surcharges when you redeem miles on its own flights.
Redemptions on partner airlines
Here are the Etihad Guest program’s partner airlines as of October 2026:
You can redeem Etihad Guest miles to fly with these airlines.
Bangkok Airways, Condor, Hong Kong Airlines, Maldivian and Starlux are recent additions to this list.
Redemptions on partner airlines are supposed to be priced according to the following award chart:
Etihad Guest partner airline award chart as of July 2025.
In practice, domestic flights operated by partner airlines often cost slightly more or fewer miles than what is shown in the table above. This is a rather frustrating “quirk” of the Etihad Guest program.
Which types of Etihad Guest rewards are the best value?
Etihad Guest redemptions are often the best value on short-haul routes.
For example, it costs only 5,000 miles to fly Economy Class on Etihad on routes under 500 miles in length. On partner airlines, it costs just 6,000 miles.
Some examples of routes under 500 miles include:
Abu Dhabi-Doha on Etihad Airways
Brussels-London on Brussels Airlines
Belgrade-Istanbul on Air Serbia
Vancouver-Calgary on Air Canada
Toronto-Montreal on Air Canada
Doha-Muscat on Oman Air
Madrid-Lisbon on TAP Air Portugal
Singapore-Kuala Lumpur on Malaysia Airlines
Colombo-Male on SriLankan Airlines or Gulf Air
Lisbon-Casablanca on Royal Air Maroc
Brussels Airlines flights within Europe can be good value when using Etihad Guest miles. Photo: Brussels Airlines.
How to book Etihad Guest award flights
You can use the Etihad website to book award flights on many partner airlines.
You can redeem miles for flights on some partner airlines on the Etihad Guest website.
To book award flights on a partner airline that isn’t available on Etihad’s website, you’ll need to call Etihad Guest. The Australian contact number is 1300 532 215.
Changing or cancelling an Etihad Guest award booking
Etihad Guest “Value” redemption bookings attract the following cancellation fees, depending on the redemption “category” booked:
More than 72 hours before departure: AED200 (~AU$80) fee for changes and no refunds available
Within 72 hours of departure: No changes or refunds available
